title: False prophets speak for profit — Jeremiah 23
paragraphs: False prophets speak for profit — Jeremiah 23
They preached for applause.
God was looking for obedience.
That is the wound inside Jeremiah 23.

False prophets were filling the air with smooth words, polished promises, profitable visions. They told people, “Peace, peace,” while judgment was already at the door. They stood in public like they carried heaven’s message, but God said they had not stood in His counsel. They ran, but He never sent them. They spoke, but He never breathed on their words.
And that still happens now.

Some voices do not fear God.
They fear losing a platform.
They fear losing donors.
They fear losing relevance.
So they soften sin, decorate compromise, and turn ministry into merchandise.
But here’s what we miss:

False prophecy is not only about wrong information.
It is also about a wrong heart.

Jeremiah 23 exposes men who used God’s name to build themselves. Profit over purity. Image over truth. Crowd over calling. And the tragedy is not only that they lied. The tragedy is that people loved lies that made them comfortable.

But God’s Word does not flatter rebellion.
It breaks it.
It burns it.
It heals it.
“Is not my word like as a fire? saith the LORD; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?” (Jeremiah 23:29)

That fire does not come to entertain you.
It comes to purify you.

That hammer does not come to amuse you.
It comes to shatter deception.
And in the middle of this chapter of warning, grace walks in.

Because Jeremiah 23 does not end with fake shepherds having the last word. God promises the Righteous Branch. A coming King from David’s line. A Shepherd who will not exploit the sheep. A Savior who will not sell the truth. His name is Jesus — “THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.”
That is the Gospel.

Where false prophets use people, Jesus lays down His life for people.
Where false prophets speak for profit, Jesus speaks truth and bleeds for sinners.
Where false shepherds scatter, Christ gathers.
Where lies condemn, Christ saves all who repent and believe.

So test every voice.
Including the ones you enjoy.

Does it exalt Christ or self?
Does it confront sin or coddle it?
Does it call for repentance or just offer inspiration?
Does it produce holiness or hype?
Do not give your soul to a voice just because it sounds confident.
Give your life to Jesus because He is true.

False prophets speak for profit.
Jesus speaks for your redemption.
